faqs.question: What is facial bojin (撥筋) as taught on The Bojin Method?
faqs.answer: Facial bojin is taught here as a gentle, hands-on face and neck self-care practice led by Taiwan-based instructor Yu-Ting Lan. It focuses on sequence, gentle placement, the supporting hand, and comfortable contact rather than scraping or forceful pressure. It is educational self-care, not medical diagnosis or treatment.

faqs.question: Do I need to buy a bojin stick before starting?
faqs.answer: No tool purchase is required to begin exploring. You can start with the free 3-step beginner reading path, the inner-brow visual guide, or the free 1:18 Above-the-Brow video demonstration, and the full course also includes a gentle fingertip start in Module 6.

faqs.question: How is facial bojin different from gua sha?
faqs.answer: Gua sha typically uses a flat edge to sweep broad areas of skin, whereas bojin uses a rounded tip with small, localized circular or linear movements along specific facial regions while using the opposite hand as a gentle supporting hand.

faqs.question: Where is the best place to start as a beginner?
faqs.answer: Begin with the free 10-second eye-area self-care observation and the 1:18 Above-the-Brow video demonstration on the Eye Reset page, or read the beginner path and safety guide to learn comfort checks and when to pause.
